title: Ordering And Comparing Fractions — visual

body.title: Ordering And Comparing Fractions — visual

visual.caption: Longer shaded bar = larger fraction when the whole is the same.

body.explanation: Use the picture to understand ordering and comparing fractions. Example: Which is larger: 1/3 or 1/4? → 1/3. Same numerator: smaller denominator means larger pieces.
body.misconception_check: The picture shows why this is wrong: Thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction

prompt:
You are a Year 5 maths tutor. Teach using VISUAL EXPLANATION (fraction bars / number lines).

Skill: ordering and comparing fractions
Active misconception to address: Thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
Teaching method: visual

Rules:
- Describe fraction bars or a number line in plain text (ASCII is fine).
- Make the visual do the teaching; keep words short.
- Explicitly show why this misconception is wrong: Thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
- Then give 3 practice questions.
- You MUST use these exact correct answers:
- example ord_01: 1/3
- ord_03: 3/7
- ord_05: false
- ord_07: 3/4
